beats.text: The horned helmet was a costume designer's idea.
beats.note: Carl Emil Doepler's designs for an 1876 production of Wagner's Ring brought it to fame.

beats.context: Viking helmet remains are known. The most complete, found in Norway in 1943 at Gjermundbu, shows no sign of ever having had horns.

beats.name: Carl Emil Doepler
beats.role: Costume designer for the Ring premiere. He studied Viking Age artefacts in museums, then took artistic freedom.

beats.note: The horned version grew from a mix of Norse and medieval German history.
Helmets of the Migration Period, 375 to 568 AD, fit the look better than anything Viking.
Lorenz Frolich's 1877 painting of Sweyn Forkbeard is described as the first known horned Viking in course literature.

beats.text: The horns came from the theatre.

beats.line: The Viking look is a nineteenth century costume.
